items.title: US and Venezuela probe secret Maduro-era oil deals

featured_image.name: Maduro-Era Oilfield Deals Face Scrutiny From US, Venezuelan Authorities -  Bloomberg

items.description:
The United States and Venezuela are scrutinizing dozens of confidential oil contracts signed during the rule of ousted leader Nicolás Maduro, according to Bloomberg, in a probe that could complicate efforts to revive the country's battered petroleum sector.[1]

The agreements, known as productive participation contracts, allowed investors to pump and trade crude oil while keeping their identities hidden to shield them from U.S. sanctions that targeted Venezuela's oil industry. The contracts also enabled Maduro's government to work with private companies despite legal restrictions on oil sales by non-state actors.[2]

Under pressure from the Trump administration, the Venezuelan government is now auditing the firms involved, while U.S. officials inspect export paperwork. Interim President Delcy Rodriguez has said there were a total of 31 such agreements, though only a handful are actively producing oil. Eight of them were pumping a combined 210,000 barrels per day on average by mid-February, according to documents reviewed by Bloomberg.[2]

items.title: China sets slowest defense budget growth since 2022 at 7%

featured_image.name: China Plans Slowest Boost to Defense Spending Since 2022 at ...

items.description: China announced a 7 percent increase in defense spending for 2026, bringing its official military budget to 1.91 trillion yuan ($277 billion), according to a Finance Ministry report released at the opening of the National People's Congress in Beijing on Thursday. The figure marks the slowest pace of growth since 2022, following three consecutive years of 7.2 percent increases.[1][2]

items.title: Zelensky says US asked Ukraine for help against Iranian drones

featured_image.name: Zelensky orders development of support plan for Middle East ...

items.description:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said on March 4 that he had spoken with leaders across the Middle East about the escalating Iran conflict and revealed that allies, including the United States, have asked Kyiv for help defending against Iranian Shahed drones — the same weapons Russia has launched tens of thousands of times against Ukrainian cities over the past four years.

In his nightly video address, Zelenskiy said he discussed the crisis with the king of Bahrain, the crown prince of Kuwait, and leaders of Jordan, Qatar, and the United Arab Emirates. "Partners are turning to us, to Ukraine, asking for help in defending against Shaheds. There have also been requests from the American side," he said, according to Reuters.[1][2]

items.title: UN says 66,000 displaced in Afghanistan-Pakistan war

featured_image.name: Nearly 66000 Afghans displaced amid fierce fighting on ... - Al Jazeera

items.description:
Nearly 66,000 people have been displaced across five eastern and southeastern Afghan provinces as a week of intense cross-border fighting between Afghanistan and Pakistan shows no signs of abating, the United Nations reported on Wednesday. The International Organization for Migration warned that "ongoing military clashes along the Durand Line have led to civilian deaths, damage to essential infrastructure, and the displacement of almost 66,000 individuals," adding that the situation risks "further displacements" in communities already stretched thin.[1][2]

The conflict, the most severe between the two neighbors in years, erupted after Pakistan launched airstrikes on Afghan territory in late February, targeting what Islamabad described as militant camps belonging to the Pakistani Taliban and the Islamic State-Khorasan Province. The Taliban-led Afghan government retaliated on February 26 with a ground offensive along the 2,640-kilometer Durand Line, prompting Pakistan to declare a state of "open war" and launch Operation Ghazab Lil Haq.[3][4]

items.title: Venezuela to reform mining law after Burgum visit

featured_image.name: Venezuela mining reform coming soon, acting president says ...

items.description:
Venezuelan acting President Delcy Rodriguez announced on Wednesday that a reform of the country's main mining legislation will be submitted to the National Assembly in the coming days, following a meeting with U.S. Interior Secretary Doug Burgum in Caracas.[1][2]

Rodriguez made the announcement after the two officials discussed investment prospects in the mining sector, including strategies to "reduce bureaucratic hurdles," according to Reuters. Burgum arrived in the South American country with mining and minerals companies that he said could represent billions in investment and thousands of jobs for Venezuela.[2][1]

items.title: Death toll tops 870 as US-Iran war spreads across Middle East

featured_image.name: Live updates: War powers vote fails in the Senate, allowing Trump to continue Iran strikes

items.description: What began on February 28 as a joint US-Israeli military campaign against Iran has rapidly metastasized into a multi-front war stretching from the Persian Gulf to the eastern Mediterranean, with more than a dozen nations now affected by the fighting. As the conflict enters its fifth day, more than 870 people have been killed across the Middle East, according to The New York Times, and diplomatic efforts to contain the violence have so far failed to gain traction.[1]

items.title: Iran conflict threatens to divert US air defense missiles from Ukraine

featured_image.name: US Army awards Patriot Advanced Capability-3 contract worth ...

items.description:
As the United States enters the fifth day of its military campaign against Iran, Ukraine faces a growing risk that the air defense missiles it depends on to repel Russian strikes will be diverted to the Middle East, where Gulf allies are scrambling to counter Iranian retaliation.

The approximately 600 PAC-3 Patriot interceptors that Lockheed Martin produces annually are already insufficient to meet the combined needs of the United States and its partners, according to a Reuters report on Tuesday. Ukraine, which relies on PAC-3 missiles to protect its energy infrastructure and military assets from Russian ballistic missiles, now finds itself competing for a finite supply with Gulf states under direct Iranian fire.[1]

items.title: Rubio pledges full US support to Turkey after NATO downs Iranian missile

featured_image.name: Rubio spoke with Turkish foreign minister and pledged full ...

items.description:
U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio pledged full American support to Turkey on Wednesday after NATO air defense systems intercepted an Iranian ballistic missile heading toward Turkish airspace, marking the first time the Western alliance has defended a member state from an Iranian projectile since the conflict between the U.S., Israel, and Iran erupted last week.

Rubio told Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan in a phone call that "the attacks on Turkey's sovereign territory were unacceptable and pledged full support from the United States," the State Department said.[1][2]

items.title: Blackout leaves two-thirds of Cuba without power as fuel crisis deepens

featured_image.name: Cuba says power slowly returning after nationwide blackout ...

items.description: An unexpected shutdown of Cuba's largest power plant plunged roughly two-thirds of the island into darkness on Wednesday, leaving nearly 7 million people without electricity as the country edges closer to what energy experts have called "zero hour" under a U.S. fuel blockade.

items.title: Iran's internet blackout hits 100 hours after US-Israeli cyberattack

featured_image.name: Iran plunged into an internet near-blackout during deepening ...

items.description: Iran has been offline for more than 100 hours and counting, after a coordinated U.S.-Israeli military and cyber offensive on February 28 triggered what cybersecurity analysts are calling the largest cyberattack in history. Internet connectivity across the country has collapsed to roughly 1 percent of normal levels, according to monitoring group NetBlocks, leaving tens of millions of Iranians cut off from the outside world.[1][2]

items.title: Gulf airports closed for fourth day as Iran conflict strands thousands

featured_image.name: Dubai International Airport Incident Injures Four

items.description: Dubai International Airport and other major Gulf aviation hubs remained closed or severely restricted for a fourth consecutive day on Wednesday, March 4, 2026, as the war between the United States, Israel, and Iran continued to shut down airspace across much of the Middle East. The closures have triggered the worst disruption to global air travel since the COVID-19 pandemic, with governments now racing to organize repatriation flights for tens of thousands of stranded passengers.[1][2]

items.title: Ecuador expels Cuba's entire embassy staff, gives 48 hours to leave

featured_image.name: Ecuador Expels Entire Cuban Embassy Staff Ahead of Trump ...

items.description: Ecuador declared Cuban Ambassador Basilio Antonio Gutiérrez García and all members of Cuba's diplomatic, consular, and administrative mission persona non grata on Wednesday, ordering them to leave the country within 48 hours. The move, announced by Ecuador's Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Human Mobility on March 4, 2026, represents one of the most dramatic diplomatic ruptures in the region in recent years.[1][2][3]

items.title: Israeli strikes kill 72 in Lebanon as diplomats back Hezbollah ban

featured_image.name: Lebanese civilians flee amid Israeli strikes on Beirut

items.description: The Quintet Committee — comprising ambassadors from Egypt, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, France, and the United States — met with Lebanese President Joseph Aoun at Baabda Palace on Tuesday to address the rapidly escalating conflict between Israel and Hezbollah, as Israeli strikes across Lebanon have now killed 72 people and displaced more than 83,000 since fighting erupted on Monday.[1][2]

items.title: Iran to allow only Chinese ships through Hormuz

featured_image.name: Oil and natural gas surge after Iran orders Strait of Hormuz closure

items.description:
Iran has announced it will permit only Chinese vessels to transit the Strait of Hormuz, describing the move as a "gesture of gratitude" for Beijing's diplomatic support since the outbreak of war with the United States and Israel, according to NDTV, which first reported the development citing sources. The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, which on Wednesday claimed "complete control" of the strait, has warned that any unauthorized vessel attempting to cross the waterway risks being struck by missiles or drones.[1][2][3]

The decision places China — the world's largest oil importer and Iran's top crude buyer — in an awkward position, caught between its economic ties to Tehran and its calls for de-escalation. Beijing has publicly urged all parties to "immediately cease military operations" and "maintain the safety of shipping lanes," according to Chinese Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning.[4][3]

items.title: Iraq suffers nationwide blackout as war disrupts gas supplies

featured_image.name: Report: Blackout Hits Central, Southern Iraq

items.description: Iraq was plunged into darkness on Wednesday evening after a sudden drop in gas supplies at a major power plant triggered a cascading failure across the country's entire electricity grid. The blackout comes as Iraq finds itself caught between warring sides in the escalating conflict between the United States, Israel, and Iran.

items.title: US and European stocks rally as oil prices stabilize

featured_image.name: Stocks rally on Fed interest rate cut hopes as 'jobless ...

items.description:
U.S. and European equities rallied on Wednesday as oil prices paused their sharp climb, offering investors a reprieve after two days of market turmoil driven by the escalating conflict between the United States, Israel, and Iran. The S&P 500 rose 0.86%, the Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 330 points, or 0.68%, and the Nasdaq Composite advanced 1.4%, according to CNN. In Europe, London's FTSE 100 rose 0.9%, Paris gained 1.1%, and Frankfurt climbed 1.5%.[1][2]

The rebound came after The New York Times reported that Iran had made indirect overtures to the United States about potential negotiations, and after Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent confirmed to CNBC that the U.S. Navy is prepared to ensure "safe passage" for oil tankers through the Strait of Hormuz "when it is appropriate and should it be needed".[3][1]

items.title: Iran has fired over 500 missiles and 2,000 drones, US military says

featured_image.name: Iran has fired more than 500 ballistic missiles, US military says - Yahoo

items.description: Iran has launched sweeping retaliatory missile and drone attacks against Israel, U.S. military installations, and Gulf Arab states, dramatically widening a conflict that began with coordinated U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iranian territory on February 28. Six American service members have been killed, dozens of civilians across the Gulf have been wounded, and the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz has sent global energy markets into turmoil.

items.title: Israel vows to assassinate Khamenei's successor as son Mojtaba reportedly chosen

featured_image.name: Mojtaba, son of Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, chosen as Iran's new ...

items.description:
Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz issued an open threat on Wednesday to assassinate whoever succeeds Ayatollah Ali Khamenei as Iran's Supreme Leader, hours after reports emerged that Khamenei's son Mojtaba had been chosen for the role. "Any leader selected by the Iranian terror regime to continue leading the plan for Israel's destruction, threatening the United States, the free world and countries in the region, and suppressing the Iranian people, will be a certain target for assassination, no matter his name or where he hides," Katz wrote in a post on X.[1][2]

Katz said he had instructed the prime minister and the Israel Defense Forces "to prepare and act by all means" to carry out the mission as part of Israel's ongoing military operation against Iran.[3][4]

items.title: New study finds sea levels far higher than assumed, raising flood risk for millions

featured_image.name: Sea level rise threatens the North Sea coast more than expected

items.description: Sea levels along the world's coastlines are much higher than scientists previously assumed — more than 3 feet higher in some regions — according to new research that suggests tens of millions more people face flooding risks from climate change than earlier assessments indicated. The findings, reported widely on Tuesday, point to a fundamental flaw in the elevation data that has underpinned decades of sea level rise planning and research.[1][2][3]

items.title: 40 years of data reveal subtle shifts in the Sun's core

featured_image.name: Scientists detect changes deep inside the Sun during solar ...

items.description:
Researchers have found that the Sun's interior subtly shifts from one quiet period to the next, a discovery that could improve forecasts of solar storms and their effects on Earth.

A team from the University of Birmingham and Yale University analyzed more than 40 years of data from the Birmingham Solar-Oscillations Network (BiSON), a chain of six telescopes positioned around the globe, to compare conditions inside the Sun during four consecutive periods of low magnetic activity known as solar minima. Their results, published in Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society, mark the first time scientists have used helioseismology — the study of sound waves trapped inside the Sun — to compare four successive minima side by side.[1][2][3][4]
